title: This LNG Stock Is Up 32% in a Year, so Why Did One Investor Sell Off a $14 Million Position?
author: Jonathan Ponciano
description: Bayberry Capital Partners fully exited its $14 million position in Golar LNG during Q4 2025, selling 346,000 shares. Despite the stock being up 32% over the past year and the company showing strong financial performance with 51% revenue growth and improving EBITDA, the fund's exit appears to be a capital allocation shift rather than a negative verdict on the company. Golar LNG benefits from long-term contracts providing multiyear earnings visibility, including a recently secured 20-year project with Argentina's Southern Energy.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company demonstrates strong financial fundamentals with 51% revenue growth, 10% EBITDA increase, and robust backlog anchored by long-term contracts including a 20-year Argentina project. Stock outperformed S&P 500 with 32% annual gain. The fund exit is characterized as a portfolio reallocation rather than a negative signal on company performance.

title: Why ServiceNow Stock Bumped Higher on Monday
author: Eric Volkman
description: ServiceNow stock rose nearly 1% on Monday after Goldman Sachs added it to its U.S. Conviction List. Goldman's analysts are bullish on ServiceNow's potential to expand into new enterprise software segments like CRM and human resources, projecting an organic CAGR of roughly 20% through 2029.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Added to Goldman Sachs' U.S. Conviction List with bullish analyst outlook. Goldman projects 20% organic CAGR through 2029 and believes the company has significant expansion potential into CRM and HR segments, leveraging its strong track record in selling to enterprise clients.

title: Satisfaction of Conditions Precedent for 20-year charter of MK II FLNG to Southern Energy in Argentina, confirming $8 billion EBITDA backlog before commodity exposure and inflationary adjustments
author: Karl Fredrik Staubo
description: Golar LNG has satisfied all conditions for a 20-year charter of its MKII FLNG to Southern Energy in Argentina, securing $8 billion in EBITDA backlog. The FLNG will be deployed in the Gulf of San Matías, with delivery expected by end of 2027 and operations starting in 2028.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Secured a long-term charter, expanded earnings visibility to 20+ years, and positioned for future growth opportunities

title: Golar LNG Limited Announces Fixed Income Investor Meetings
author: Golar Lng Limited
description: Golar LNG Limited plans to issue USD benchmark senior unsecured notes through a syndicate of banks, with investor meetings starting September 22, 2025. The offering is subject to market conditions and will be made to qualified institutional buyers.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company is pursuing a standard capital markets transaction to raise funds, with no overtly positive or negative indicators in the announcement. The offering is contingent on market conditions, reflecting a balanced approach to financing.

title: Golar LNG Gains $13.7 Billion Backlog
author: Jesterai
description: Golar LNG reported strong Q2 2025 earnings, securing $13.7 billion in EBITDA backlog, executing new twenty-year charters, and raising $575 million through convertible bonds while maintaining a robust financial position.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company demonstrated strong financial performance with a $13.7 billion EBITDA backlog, successful long-term charters, strategic financial maneuvers like convertible bond issuance and share buybacks, and potential for significant future free cash flow growth
